detail.title: Mechanisms of Autocatalytic Memory
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on how non-templated reaction networks can maintain history-dependent states. Evidence suggests that stoichiometric constraints, specifically those derived from the network's S-matrix, can enable multistable attractors. These attractors allow a system to 'remember' its prior exposure to environmental conditions, distinct from simple templated information storage.
detail.reason: Updating to incorporate structural network constraints and simulated environmental adaptation as foundational evidence for memory mechanisms.
